name: Stokely Carmichael
milestone_by_age_26: Elected chairman of SNCC in May 1966 at age 24 and popularized the 'Black Power' slogan during the March Against Fear in June 1966, becoming a national civil rights figure.
early_history_summary: Carmichael immigrated from Trinidad to New York at age 11 and attended the elite Bronx High School of Science. He joined civil rights protests as a high school senior in 1960, participated in Freedom Rides in 1961, and became a full-time SNCC organizer after graduating from Howard University in 1964, leading voter registration efforts in Mississippi and Alabama.
family_context_summary: Born in Port-of-Spain, Trinidad to a steamship stewardess mother and carpenter father who immigrated to New York when he was 2, leaving him with grandparents until age 11; family was working-class, with his mother working as a maid.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite school, civil rights movement, mentorship, adversity, lived experience
evidence_summary: Carmichael leveraged access to elite education (Bronx High School of Science, Howard University) and the civil rights movement's infrastructure to become a national figure by 24. His working-class immigrant background and direct experience of racial injustice fueled his commitment. Mentored by Ella Baker and Bob Moses, he rose through SNCC's ranks through sustained organizing in the Deep South.
starting_point: Born in Port-of-Spain, Trinidad to a carpenter father and steamship stewardess mother who immigrated to New York when he was 2, leaving him with grandparents until age 11.
current_position: Died November 15, 1998 in Conakry, Guinea at age 57; final role: leader of the All-African People's Revolutionary Party.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at Howard University and joined SNCC's Nonviolent Action Group.
Participated as a Freedom Rider in Mississippi and was arrested for the first time.
Graduated from Howard University and joined SNCC full-time for Freedom Summer in Mississippi.
Elected chairman of SNCC in May 1966 and popularized the 'Black Power' slogan during the March Against Fear in June.
Published 'Black Power: The Politics of Liberation' and stepped down as SNCC chairman.
Became Honorary Prime Minister of the Black Panther Party before breaking with the group.
Relocated to Guinea, changed his name to Kwame Ture, and devoted himself to pan-African activism.
Died of prostate cancer in Conakry, Guinea.

name: Michael Hester
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Hester took his first refereeing course in 1994 at age 22 but only committed to refereeing full-time at 28 in 2001, with FIFA listing in 2007 and World Cup selection in 2010.
early_history_summary: Hester played rugby and football before taking a refereeing course at age 22 in 1994. He continued playing while refereeing low-level matches and only committed to refereeing full-time at age 28 in 2001, rising rapidly through the ranks to earn a FIFA listing in 2007.
evidence_summary: Hester's refereeing career began at 22 but his major achievements (FIFA listing, World Cup) came well after age 26. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Győző Kulcsár
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic team gold medal in épée at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 24, the first of three consecutive Olympic team titles.
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest, Kulcsár lived in Germany and Sweden during WWII before returning to Hungary in 1946. He started fencing at age 15 in 1955 and competed for Dózsa Újpest from 1957. He joined the Hungarian national team in 1962 at age 22 and won Olympic team gold two years later.
family_context_summary: Born in Budapest in 1940; family lived in Germany and Sweden during WWII before returning to Hungary in 1946. No details on family financial status or occupation.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian fencing pipeline, national team, club system, mentor coach
evidence_summary: Kulcsár benefited from Hungary's elite fencing pipeline, starting at 15 and joining the national team by 22. His mentor Vass Imre provided sustained individualized training. The Hungarian épée team was among the world's best, providing a high-trust competitive environment. Wartime displacement in childhood added adversity.
starting_point: Born in Budapest, Hungary in 1940; family displaced to Germany and Sweden during WWII before returning to Hungary in 1946.
current_position: Died September 19, 2018 in Budapest at age 77; final role: head coach of the Hungarian épée team and member of the FIE Hall of Fame.

trajectory.event: Started fencing at age 15 in Hungary.
Began competing for Dózsa Újpest fencing club.
Became member of the Hungarian national fencing team and competed at World Championships in Buenos Aires.
Won Olympic team gold in épée at the Tokyo Olympics.
Won both individual and team Olympic gold in épée at the Mexico City Olympics.
Won Olympic team gold and individual bronze in épée at the Munich Olympics.
Retired from competition and became secretary-general of the Hungarian Fencing Association.
Died on September 19, 2018 in Budapest.

name: Mohammed Emwazi
milestone_by_age_26: No positive material milestone by age 26; Emwazi graduated with a computing degree in 2009 and worked as an IT salesman. His notoriety as 'Jihadi John' began in 2014 at age 26, but this is infamy from terrorist acts, not a positive achievement.
early_history_summary: Born in Kuwait to a stateless Bidoon family, Emwazi moved to London at age 6. He attended Quintin Kynaston School and graduated from the University of Westminster in 2009 with a degree in Information Systems with Business Management, then worked as an IT salesman in Kuwait.
family_context_summary: Born in Kuwait to a stateless Bidoon family of Iraqi origin; family moved to the UK in 1994 and settled in inner west London, living in subsidised accommodation.
evidence_summary: Emwazi had no positive material milestone by age 26. He completed a computing degree in 2009 and worked as an IT salesman. His notoriety as 'Jihadi John' from ISIS execution videos in 2014 is infamy from terrorism, not a positive achievement.

name: Legna Verdecia
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship gold in the 52 kg category at the 1993 World Judo Championships in Hamilton at age 21, and added Olympic bronze at the 1996 Atlanta Games at age 24.
early_history_summary: Verdecia started judo at age 13 in 1985 in Holguín, Cuba, after being recruited by a coach. She was quickly talent-spotted for Cuba's EIDE sports school, winning her first national gold at age 13. She won World Junior Championship gold in 1990 at age 18 and Pan American Games gold in 1991 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Manzanillo, Granma, Cuba; family moved to Holguín when she was about 2 years old. Father was supportive of her sports activities. No details on family financial status.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban sports system, EIDE, early talent identification, judo specialization
evidence_summary: Verdecia was talent-spotted at 13 and entered Cuba's elite sports pipeline (EIDE), which provided structured training, coaching, and competition access. The Cuban national sports system supported her full-time athletic development. She progressed rapidly from national school competitions to World Junior Champion at 18 and World Champion at 21.
starting_point: Born in Manzanillo, Granma, Cuba on October 29, 1972; family moved to Holguín province as a toddler; father worked in Santiago de Cuba.
current_position: Retired from competitive judo in 2006; lives in Cuba; recognized as one of the most successful Cuban judoka in history with 165 wins out of 187 fights.

trajectory.event: Started judo training and was quickly recruited to Cuba's EIDE sports school.
Won World Junior Championship gold in the 48 kg category in Dijon, France.
Won World Championship gold in the 52 kg category in Hamilton, Canada.
Won Olympic bronze medal in the 52 kg category at the Atlanta Olympics.
Won Olympic gold medal in the 52 kg category at the Sydney Olympics.
Retired from competitive judo.

name: Lucile Wheeler
milestone_by_age_26: Won Canada's first Olympic ski medal, a bronze in downhill, at the 1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics at age 21, and became World Champion in downhill and giant slalom at the 1958 World Championships at age 23.
early_history_summary: Wheeler grew up at her family's Gray Rocks ski resort in Sainte-Jovite, Quebec, built by her grandfather. She was on skis by age 2, coached by the resort's ski school director Herman Gadner, and won the Canadian junior ski championship at age 12. Her parents funded several winters of training in Kitzbühel, Austria with coach Pepi Salvenmoser.
family_context_summary: Born into a family that owned the Gray Rocks ski centre at Mont-Tremblant, Quebec, built by her grandfather George Wheeler. Her father Harry Wheeler owned and operated the resort and competed at the 1932 Lake Placid Olympics in dogsled racing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather built the Gray Rocks ski centre; father Harry Wheeler owned the resort and was an athlete himself, competing at the 1932 Lake Placid Olympics. Family was deeply embedded in the ski industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family ski resort, grandfather built resort, early coaching, European training, ski immersion
evidence_summary: Wheeler's family owned the Gray Rocks ski centre, giving her on-snow access from age 2 and professional coaching from the resort's ski school director. Her father, himself an Olympian, funded multiple winters of elite training in Kitzbühel, Austria. This combination of family-domain immersion, capital support, and dedicated coaching made her one of the first North Americans to break Europe's alpine skiing monopoly.
starting_point: Born January 14, 1935 in Sainte-Jovite, Quebec to the Wheeler family, owners of the Gray Rocks ski centre at Mont-Tremblant; grandfather George Wheeler built the resort after emigrating from New York.
current_position: Retired from racing in 1959; resides in Quebec's Eastern Townships; age 90; inducted into Canadian and U.S. Ski Halls of Fame and carried the flag at the 1988 Calgary Winter Olympics opening ceremony.

trajectory.event: Entered her first ski race at Mont Tremblant, finishing seventh in a field open to all ages.
Won the Canadian junior ski championship.
Competed at the Oslo Winter Olympics, placing 26th in slalom.
Won Canada's first Olympic ski medal, a bronze in downhill, at the Cortina d'Ampezzo Winter Olympics.
Won World Championship gold in both downhill and giant slalom, becoming the first North American world champion in downhill.
Retired from competitive racing and made instructional ski videos.
Appointed Officer of the Order of Canada.
Served as Olympic flagbearer at the Calgary Winter Games opening ceremony.

name: Jean-Jacques Annaud
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Annaud graduated from IDHEC film school in 1964 at age 21 and directed advertising films in the late 1960s, but his first feature film was 'Black and White in Color' in 1976 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Annaud was educated at the technical school in Vaugirard and graduated from IDHEC film school in Paris in 1964. He directed television advertisements in Africa and France in the late 1960s to early 1970s before making his first feature film at 33.
family_context_summary: Born in Draveil, Essonne, France to Pierre and Madeleine Annaud. No details on family financial status.
evidence_summary: Annaud graduated from IDHEC film school at 21 and directed advertising films through his twenties, but his first feature film and Oscar win came at 33 in 1976. No material milestone by 26 was found.

name: Claudia Bokel
milestone_by_age_26: Became World Junior Champion in épée in 1992 at age 19, and competed at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics at age 23, placing 9th individually and 7th with the team.
early_history_summary: Bokel started fencing at age 7, following her older siblings. At 16, she moved alone from the Netherlands to Bonn, Germany to attend a boarding school attached to the Olympischer Fechtclub Bonn, a fencing academy that produced numerous Olympic athletes. She became World Junior Champion after just three years there.
family_context_summary: Born in Ter Apel, Netherlands; her father gave her permission to start fencing at age 7 after watching older siblings fence. Family supported her move to Germany at 16 for fencing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Older brother and sister both fenced, creating a family fencing environment. Father approved and supported her fencing career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: OFC Bonn fencing school, sibling fencing, early start, German national pipeline
evidence_summary: Bokel started fencing at 7 following her older siblings and moved alone to Germany at 16 to join the elite OFC Bonn fencing boarding school. The national coach Manfred Kaspar identified her talent and recruited her. This concentrated training environment produced a World Junior Championship in just three years, followed by three Olympic appearances.
starting_point: Born August 30, 1973 in Ter Apel, Netherlands to a family where her older brother and sister both fenced; father supported her fencing from age 7.
current_position: Retired from competitive fencing in 2008; served as IOC Executive Board member (2012-2016) and president of the German Fencing Association (2016); works as a senior consultant at Bayer Leverkusen.

trajectory.event: Started fencing at age 7, following her older siblings.
Moved alone from the Netherlands to Bonn, Germany to attend the OFC Bonn fencing boarding school.
Became World Junior Champion in épée.
Competed at the Atlanta Olympics, placing 9th individually and 7th with the team.
Won World Championship gold in the individual épée event in Nancy, France.
Won Olympic team silver medal in épée at the Athens Olympics.
Elected to the IOC Athletes' Commission and retired from competitive fencing.
Elected president of the German Fencing Association.

name: Kiki Camarena
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Camarena graduated high school in 1966, served in the Marines (1968-70), and worked as a fireman and police officer before joining the DEA in 1974 at age 27. His fame came from his assassination in 1985.
early_history_summary: Born in Mexicali, Mexico, Camarena's family immigrated to Calexico, California when he was a child. The family endured poverty. He graduated high school in 1966, joined the Marines in 1968, then worked as a fireman and police officer before joining the DEA in 1974.
family_context_summary: Born in Mexicali, Mexico; family immigrated to Calexico, California when he was a child and endured considerable poverty. Parents divorced when he was young. His oldest brother died serving in Vietnam in 1965.
evidence_summary: Camarena had no material milestone by age 26. He was a Marine and then a local police officer in his early twenties before joining the DEA at 27. His fame came from his kidnapping and murder by the Guadalajara Cartel in 1985 at age 37.

name: Shane Warne
milestone_by_age_26: Made Test debut for Australia against India in January 1992 at age 22, and bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting in the 1993 Ashes series at age 23, establishing himself as a rising star in international cricket.
early_history_summary: Warne grew up in Melbourne's outer suburbs and won a sports scholarship to Mentone Grammar. He joined the Australian cricket academy at 19, made his first-class debut for Victoria in 1991 at 22, and was selected for Australia's Test team the same season after just seven Sheffield Shield matches.
family_context_summary: Born in Upper Ferntree Gully, Victoria, a suburb of Melbourne, to Keith and Brigitte Warne. His mother was German. He attended Hampton High School before winning a sports scholarship to Mentone Grammar.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having cricket-specific family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian cricket academy, sports scholarship, Sheffield Shield, national team selection
evidence_summary: Warne leveraged Australia's elite cricket pipeline, winning a sports scholarship to Mentone Grammar and joining the national cricket academy at 19. Despite limited first-class experience (only 7 matches), he was fast-tracked into the Test team at 22. His natural leg-spin talent, a dying art in cricket, set him apart. Early career struggles with fitness and form nearly derailed him before his breakthrough in the 1993 Ashes.
starting_point: Born September 13, 1969 in Upper Ferntree Gully, Victoria, a suburb of Melbourne, to Keith and Brigitte Warne; won a sports scholarship to Mentone Grammar school.
current_position: Died March 4, 2022 on Ko Samui, Thailand at age 52; widely regarded as one of the greatest cricketers of all time with 708 Test wickets.

trajectory.event: Joined the Australian national cricket academy in Adelaide.
Made first-class debut for Victoria and played just seven Sheffield Shield matches before Test selection.
Made Test debut for Australia against India at the Sydney Cricket Ground in January 1992.
Bowled the 'Ball of the Century' to Mike Gatting in the first Test of the 1993 Ashes series at Old Trafford.
Led Australia to World Cup victory as a key bowler.
Became the first bowler to take 700 Test wickets.
Retired from Test cricket with 708 wickets in 145 Tests.
Died of a suspected heart attack on Ko Samui, Thailand.

name: Kaija Saariaho
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Saariaho studied graphic design and musicology before beginning composition studies at the Sibelius Academy in 1976. Her first publicly performed student composition was 'Bruden' in 1977 at age 25, but her professional breakthrough came in the 1980s at IRCAM.
early_history_summary: Saariaho played violin, guitar, and piano growing up in Helsinki. She studied graphic design and musicology before turning to composition at the Sibelius Academy in 1976 under Paavo Heininen. Her early student works were performed at Sibelius Academy concerts in the late 1970s, but her professional career began after moving to Paris and IRCAM in 1982.
family_context_summary: Born in Helsinki, Finland to Launo Laakkonen, an industrialist who created his own business in the metal industry, and his wife Tuovi. The family lived in Helsinki and had a summer house in Karelia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an industrialist/inventor in the metal industry; no documented musical family background.
evidence_summary: Saariaho had no material professional milestone by age 26. She was still a composition student at the Sibelius Academy, with only student works performed at student concerts. Her professional breakthrough came in the 1980s after moving to IRCAM in Paris.

name: Giorgio Moroder
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Moroder began touring Europe as a musician at 18 and released singles from 1963, but his first hit ('Looky Looky') came in 1969 at age 29, and his first hit as a composer (Ricky Shayne's 'Ich sprenge alle Ketten') was in 1968 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Moroder taught himself guitar at 15, inspired by Paul Anka. At 18, he began touring Europe as a professional musician, performing at night and recording during the day. He moved to Berlin around 1965 and released singles under the name 'Giorgio' from 1963, but achieved no notable commercial success before age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Urtijëi, South Tyrol, Italy to Ladin parents; his father was a hotel concierge. He grew up in a mixed Ladin-, Italian- and German-speaking environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Came from a family of creative artists; one brother is artist Ulrich Moroder. No documented music industry family background.
evidence_summary: Moroder had no material milestone by age 26. He was touring and releasing singles from his early twenties but had no commercial hits. His first hit as a composer was in 1968 at age 28, and his first hit as a recording artist was 'Looky Looky' in 1969 at age 29.
